title: Standardize crypto abstraction and migrate SSO stack to maintained libs
creator: Avery Patel
body:
Summary:
We need to reduce tech debt and security risk by consolidating Redwood's crypto/SSO dependency surface. This ticket standardizes a lightweight crypto abstraction layer, upgrades OpenSSL bindings, and migrates legacy SAML/OAuth/JWT adapters to actively maintained libraries. The goal is to remove brittle, internal glue code, fix multiple CVE exposures in older deps, and enable deterministic build matrices for private deployments.

Scope (what this ticket covers):
- Add a single CryptoAdapter interface (in rust/crypto) and migrate callers in auth-service, runtime, and private installer.
- Replace legacy saml-adapter (internal fork) with passport-saml v7 equivalent integration via a compatibility shim for existing config.
- Bump jwt-lib to up-to-date release (node-jose -> jose v4) and audit token parsing paths for vulnerable algorithms (e.g., reject none, HS256 fallback).
- Upgrade OpenSSL system bindings used by the runtime (openssl-sys -> openssl 0.11, bump CMake flags for FIPS compatibility where present).
- Add CI fuzz tests for JWT parsing and SAML assertion handling; add regression tests for token expiry and algorithm enforcement.

Out-of-scope for this ticket (handled by follow-ups):
- Full migration of the old SSO admin UI components (separate frontend ticket).
- On-prem packaging changes for older OS distro backports (will be follow-up with installer team).

Why now:
- Security review flagged multiple transitive dependencies with known CVEs during the Q1 audit.
- Customer requests for stronger KMS and audit trail guarantees make this a P0 remediation.

Acceptance criteria:
1) All production services compile against the new CryptoAdapter and no longer import the legacy internal crypto helpers.
2) OpenSSL bindings upgraded and CI runs integration tests on both Linux/Ubuntu 22.04 and CentOS-7 (where we still build for on-prem).
3) SAML flows pass the end-to-end test harness (idp simulator) with signed assertions and relay state preserved.
4) JWT parsing rejects insecure algorithm choices and tokens with malformed headers; CI coverage added.
5) Rolling deploy/runbook documented and validated in staging; all rollbacks automated via the rollout policy.

Migration strategy and rollout plan:
- Phase 1 (dev branch): Implement CryptoAdapter and shims to allow side-by-side usage. Add feature flags for new libs.
- Phase 2 (staging): Flip feature flags for non-critical internal traffic; run integration harness that simulates customer SSO flows.
- Phase 3 (canary): Canary on 2% of hosted traffic with automatic rollback on auth error spike (>0.5% delta) or latency regressions (>30ms p95 increase).
- Phase 4 (general): Gradual ramp to 100% with monitoring for metrics outlined below. Coordinate Dedicated/Private customers for maintenance windows.

Instrumentation and monitoring additions:
- New auth-service metrics: saml_assertion_validation_failures, jwt_decode_errors_by_reason, crypto_adapter_fallbacks.
- Dashboards in Console: per-route latency for /auth/* and percentage of requests using new adapter.
- Alerts: page on >5% auth failures in canary window or any increase in error rate lasting >5m.

Testing plan:
- Unit tests for CryptoAdapter edge cases and key parse logic.
- Fuzz targets for JWT header/body parsing covering algorithm fields, nested JSON, and oversized headers.
- SAML E2E against idp-sim v2 including signed assertion validation, clock skew scenarios, and replay detection.
- Integration smoke tests in runtime-compat pipeline and post-deploy smoke in staging.

Backward compatibility and customer migrations:
- Provide a compatibility shim mapping legacy config keys to new library options.
- For customers on Dedicated/Private, include an opt-in compatibility flag in the console and a migration checklist for on-prem installers.

Notes on trade-offs and decisions so far:
- We chose a minimal abstraction rather than a large rewrite to keep the risk window small. That means a temporary shim layer will exist for ~2 sprints.
- Decided to use jose v4 for JWT parsing due to active maintenance and type safety; added token validation wrapper to centralize algorithm whitelisting.
- For SAML, selected passport-saml fork alignment because it supports our ACS/relay-state patterns with minimal shim code; heavy frontend admin changes deferred.

Implementation artifacts and links:
- Proposal doc: https://docs.redwood-inference.com/confluence/SEC-CRYPTO-2026
- Runtime PR (crypto adapter): https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-runtime/pull/4821
- Auth-service PR (saml + jwt): https://github.com/redwood-inference/auth-service/pull/318
- CI fuzz suite commit: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ci-tools/commit/9f3b2a7

Follow-ups (create new tickets after merge):
- Frontend admin migration for SSO settings (PM + DES tickets).
- Packaging backport for older on-prem images.
- Post-release dependency sweep for transitive crates/npm packages.

Owner notes (for assignee):
- Start by running the staging harness locally (scripts/auth-harness) and get green on idp-sim tests before touching runtime bindings.
- Coordinate with infra to open a short maintenance window for canary rollout to Dedicated clusters.
- Prepare a short migration email template for affected enterprise customers (work with Solutions).
acceptance_criteria: CryptoAdapter in master with shims and no production imports of legacy crypto helpers
OpenSSL bindings upgraded and CI green on supported distros
SAML end-to-end harness passing with signed assertions
JWT parser rejects insecure algorithms and has fuzz coverage
Rollout runbook documented and canary test completed in staging
migration_steps: Create CryptoAdapter and implement shims for auth-service and runtime
Integrate jose v4 JWT parser and centralize token validation policies
Replace internal saml-adapter with compatibility shim to passport-saml equivalent
Bump openssl crate bindings and re-run build matrix for all platforms
Add CI fuzz tests and add auth-related alerts to Console
test_plan: Unit tests for adapter and token validation wrapper
SAML E2E with idp-sim covering replay and clock skew
Staging canary traffic validation and smoke tests
risks: Temporary regression in auth latency during adapter initialization; mitigate with warm-start caches
Compatibility gaps with older customer SSO configurations — will ship compatibility shim and migration docs
Edge-case JWTs (nested JWTs / custom alg) causing rejection — add allow-list and migration warning logs

2026-03-03 Jordan Liu: Spike completed — CryptoAdapter interface prototype works, jwt/lib evaluation results attached. Recommending jose v4 and openssl 0.11.
2026-03-05 Security Review (Marisol Gomez): Reviewed threat model. Request to add algorithm enforcement and callback for custom KMS. Marked security_review_required=true.
2026-03-08 Jordan Liu: Opened runtime PR #4821 (crypto adapter). CI failing on CentOS-7 build due to older OpenSSL dev headers. Working with infra to add backport job.
2026-03-10 DevOps (Ethan Moore): Added backport builder for CentOS-7 in CI; build green for openssl binding matrix.
2026-03-12 QA (Priya Desai): Staging harness results: SAML E2E green for ACS flows; found one edge case with RelayState length >2048 bytes, added additional handling.
